news.title: No more Messi nights for Argentina as skipper says adios to national squad
news.lede: Fifa president Gianni Infantino led the tributes to Argentina skipper Lionel Messi, who announced his retirement from international football just over a month after playing in the 2026 World Cup final. "Thank you for bringing so much joy to millions of football fans," said Infantino, who handed Messi a runners-up medal following his side's 1-0 defeat to Spain on 19 July at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. "You are retiring from international football as one of the greatest players our sport has ever seen. I wish you all the best."

news.title: Under-fire South Korean FA hires ex-Spain boss Robert Moreno as interim coach
news.lede: South Korea’s beleaguered football association on Tuesday appointed former Spain boss Robert Moreno as interim coach, following a disastrous World Cup and series of damaging controversies. Moreno, who was forced to deny earlier this year during a stint in Russia that he used ChatGPT to prepare for games, will be in charge for friendly games in September-October. South Korea will compete in the Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia from January 7 to February 5. The Korea Football Association (KFA) said Moreno could lead the team at the Asian Cup, “subject to an evaluation” of his performance.

news.title: Why Messi’s legacy extends beyond the game itself
news.lede: Argentine genius Lionel Messi retired from international football on Monday.It was not unexpected. He had been dropping hints post his World Cup heartbreak, hints that grew stronger after his father passed away.The 39-year-old said he had nothing more to give. He had given everything for Argentina. Despite having learnt football in Spain, he had famously turned down the chance to represent the European giants on the world stage.
